description: Interactive matching activity for Grade 7 Mathematics — Sign Rules Matcher. Students drag eight integer multiplication expressions to either a 'Positive Result' bin or a 'Negative Result' bin. Expressions cover all four sign cases. Instant feedback after each placement. Summary card with complete sign rule on completion.
topic: Operations with Integers — Patterns with Negative Multiplicand and Complete Sign Rules
textbook_reference: Ganita Prakash Grade 7 Part-II, Chapter 2: Operations with Integers, Section 2.2
learning_objectives: Determine the sign of a product without computing the value
Recall that same-sign multiplication yields a positive result
Recall that different-sign multiplication yields a negative result
Connect (−1) × a = −a to the additive inverse property
Bridge multiplication sign rules to division sign rules

expressions.description: Custom set of multiplication expressions. Each has id, display text, sign parts, and correct bin.

summaryRule.default: Same signs → Positive  |  Different signs → Negative

instructionText.default: Drag each expression to the correct bin. Determine the sign of the result — no calculation needed!

default_8_expressions.description: Default set covering all four sign cases with tricky examples

division_sign_rules.description: Same activity but for division — bridging from multiplication

additionalProps.instructionText: Division follows the same sign rules as multiplication! Sort each expression.
You do NOT need to calculate — just determine whether the product is positive or negative!

teaching_notes.purpose: This tool tests active recall of the sign rule after the pattern-based derivation in the textbook (Ganita Prakash Ch.2). Students classify expressions by sign without computing exact values.
key_teaching_moments: Expressions e5 (−1)×(−1) and e6 (−1)×(+5) are deliberately included: (−1)×(−1) = +1 surprises many students; (−1)×(+5) = −5 connects to the additive inverse property (−1 × a = −a).
After the activity, ask: 'Can you now state the sign rule for multiplication in one sentence without looking?'
Bridge to division: 'Do you think division follows the same rule? Why?' — then optionally load the division variant.
prerequisite_knowledge: Addition and subtraction of integers (Grade 6 recap)
Token model for integer multiplication (positive multiplier placing tokens, negative multiplier removing tokens)
Pattern observation: decreasing multiplier with positive/negative multiplicand
common_misconceptions: Students may think (−1)×(−1) is negative because both numbers 'look' negative
Confusing the sign of the result with the sign of the larger number
Applying addition rules (same sign = add, different sign = subtract) to multiplication

instructions_for_student: Drag each multiplication expression to the correct bin — Positive Result (+) or Negative Result (−). You do NOT need to calculate the exact answer, just determine the sign. After each placement you will see if you are right. Once all 8 are correctly placed, a summary card shows you the complete sign rule.

design_spec.layout: Top half: row of shuffled expression cards in Lilita One font. Bottom half: two bins side-by-side — left green-bordered 'Positive Result (+)' and right red-bordered 'Negative Result (−)'. Cards styled like CBSE exam question slips.

feedback.correct: Card snaps into bin with green tick animation (0.3s bounce)
feedback.wrong: Card shakes back to row with red flash

design_spec.summary_card: Slides up from bottom after all 8 correct: 'Same signs → Positive | Different signs → Negative' with colour-coded rows. Includes Brahmagupta historical note.
design_spec.font: Lilita One for headings/cards, Nunito for body
design_spec.interaction: Mouse-drag and touch-tap both supported. Mobile-responsive with wrapping cards on small screens.
